+        +----------------+---------------------+---------------------+
+        | ``logcdf(x)``  | -inf                | 0                   |
+        +----------------+---------------------+---------------------+
+        | ``ccdf(x)``    | 1                   | 0                   |
+        +----------------+---------------------+---------------------+

+    @abstractmethod
+    def moment(self, order, kind, *, method):
+        r"""Raw, central, or standard moment of positive integer order.
+

+        :math:`\chi`, the "raw" moment (about the origin) of order :math:`n` of
+        a random variable :math:`X` is:

+

+        :math:`\mu = \mu'_1`:
+
+        .. math::
+
+            \mu_n(X) = \int_{\chi} (x - \mu) ^n f(x) dx

+        :math:`n^\text{th}` power of the standard deviation
+        :math:`\sigma = \sqrt{\mu_2}` to produce a scale invariant quantity:

+        .. math::

+        variance

problem_statement: Pull request #21700: ENH: `stats.Mixture`: add mixture distributions for new infrastructure #### What does this implement/fix? This adds `scipy.stats.Mixture`, a class for mixture distributions. *Update: Don't be scared by the line count; almost all of it is just movement of documentation.* ```python3 import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from scipy.stats import Mixture, Normal vars = (Normal(mu=-1.2, sigma=1.1), Normal(mu=1.3, sigma=0.9)) weights = (0.4, 0.6) X = Mixture(vars, weights=weights) x = np.linspace(-5, 5, 300) plt.plot(x, X.pdf(x)) plt.hist(X.sample(10000), density=True, bins=30) plt.show() ``` #### Additional information Questions: - ~~What should the class be called?~~ People seem happy with `Mixture`. - ~~What should the arguments be called? Should the random variables and their probabilities be separate lists (as they are now) or, say, a list of tuples?~~ People seem happy with separate `components` (positional only) and `weights`. - ~~To avoid copy-pasting all the method documentation, I was thinking that this and `ContinuousDistribution` should be a subclass of a new superclass `StatisticalDistribution`, and method documentation would go there. Of course, there will be several other subclasses, like `DiscreteDistribution`, etc. Should that superclass be created in this PR or shall we do a separate PR and rebase this after that merges?~~ I'd like to add `_ProbabilityDistribution` in this PR. Thoughts: - There are many ways of making this more efficient at the cost of extra complexity. Let's keep this simple. - Currently this is only for distributions with scalar shapes (not arrays). Separate PR can extend to array shapes. - I remember a request for zero-inflated distributions. I'd like to enable this by creating a degenerate/Dirac continuous distribution in a follow-up PR. The obvious alternative is to wait until there is a discrete uniform distribution (which could have all its mass at zero). - When there are discrete distributions in the mixture, I suppose the PDF at the support values of the discrete distributions will be infinite? And perhaps this class should _also_ have a PMF method, and the PMF at values that are not in the support of a discrete distribution would be zero? - I'll probably want to test edge behavior with distributions that have finite support (but it doesn't really matter until these are public). - `mode` may not return the global maximum of the PDF. This is [already documented](https://scipy.github.io/devdocs/reference/generated/scipy.stats.Normal.mode.html#scipy.stats.Normal.mode). - See gh-21707, which would allow mixtures to be composed of most existing continuous distributions. With that, supersedes gh-19413.
